2026 · Environmental Research · Universitas Sumatera Utara

Microplastic Contamination in Agricultural Soil

A study of potential microplastic contamination in chili agricultural land associated with plastic mulch use

Field SamplingLab AnalysisExcelSPSSScientific Research

Problem

Plastic mulch is widely used in agricultural practices, but its degradation and fragmentation may contribute to microplastic contamination in agricultural soil. This study investigated the potential presence of microplastics in chili-growing agricultural land and explored their relationship with selected soil-quality parameters.

Workflow

Soil Sampling → Sample Preparation → Microplastic Identification → Soil Quality Analysis → Data Processing → Statistical Analysis → Polymer Confirmation → Report Writing

Key Findings

  • Mulched soils showed higher microplastic abundance than non-mulched soil — average 6,520 particles/kg vs 2,000 particles/kg, a 226% increase.
  • Film-shaped, black microplastics were predominant, indicating degraded plastic mulch as a major contributor.
  • Raman analysis identified Polyethylene (PE) and Polypropylene (PP) as the main polymers, likely from plastic mulch and twine.
  • Microplastic footprint ranged from 28,224 to 2.8 million particles/kg of chili.

Clean Water Distribution Map

Self-initiated GIS project

GISSpatial Analysis

Project Overview

A self-initiated GIS project created to practice spatial analysis for an environmental infrastructure context. The project explores the distribution and potential service coverage of clean-water facilities using spatial data and buffer analysis.

Why I Built This

To strengthen practical GIS skills and explore how spatial analysis can be applied to environmental infrastructure and clean-water accessibility.

My Contribution

I independently prepared the spatial data, performed GIS processing and buffer analysis, developed the map visualization, and interpreted the resulting spatial patterns.

Workflow

  • Input Data — imported PDAM coordinates from Google Maps (CSV) and river shapefile into QGIS.
  • Reprojection — all layers reprojected to EPSG:32647 (UTM 47N).
  • Buffer Analysis — PDAM network: 3 km & 7 km · River: 500 m & 1.5 km.
  • Spatial Join — buffers merged into the sub-district layer for scoring.
  • Scoring — total score = PDAM score + river score (Field Calculator).
  • Classification & Visualization — graduated symbology, 3 classes, exported at 300 dpi.

Key Finding

Western and southern areas — limited access. Several areas in western and southern Deli Serdang received lower accessibility scores, primarily based on distance from existing PDAM facilities and the availability of major river systems.

Policy recommendations. Prioritize the improvement and expansion of existing PDAM infrastructure to increase distribution capacity and service coverage in areas with limited access. Where network expansion is challenging, explore suitable river sources as raw-water sources, supported by small-scale clean-water treatment facilities where feasible.

Disclaimer: The accessibility assessment is based on the availability and spatial distribution of PDAM and clean-water facilities within the predefined scoring criteria used in this GIS model. The resulting scores represent a spatial modelling exercise and have not been validated through field surveys. Actual water accessibility, infrastructure capacity, raw-water availability, and local conditions may differ from the results presented.
